Nine functions in `lib/response.js` and one in `lib/router/index.js` call `res.set` directly. I found them by searching `lib/` for every `.set(` and `.header(` call, then matching each line to the function that contains it.

**`lib/response.js`** (all call `this.set(...)`):
- `res.links`: sets `Link` (line 94).
- `res.send`: sets `Content-Type`, `Content-Length` and `ETag` (lines 175–223).
- `res.json`: sets `Content-Type` (line 276).
- `res.jsonp`: sets `X-Content-Type-Options` and `Content-Type` (lines 320–332).
- `res.type` / `res.contentType`: sets `Content-Type` (line 625). It's one function under two names, listed below as `contentType`.
- `res.format`: sets `Content-Type` inside its body (line 699).
- `res.attachment`: sets `Content-Disposition` (line 725).
- `res.append`: sets the field it was given (line 756).
- `res.location`: sets `Location` (line 924).
- `res.redirect`: sets `Content-Length` (line 982).

**`lib/router/index.js`**:
- `sendOptionsResponse`: calls `res.set('Allow', body)` (line 654).

I left out three things:
- The call at line 798 is inside `res.set` itself.
- The `this.set(...)` calls in `lib/application.js` are `app.set`.
- Matches on `res.set(...)` in doc comments (lines 641 and 765–767) aren't real calls.

A search for bracket access (`res['set']`) and `set.call` / `set.apply` turned up nothing more.
